questions.stem: Shape $A$ has vertices at $(1,1)$, $(3,1)$, and $(1,3)$. Shape $B$ has vertices at $(1,-1)$, $(3,-1)$, and $(1,-3)$. Describe the single transformation that maps $A$ to $B$.
questions.explanation: Each $y$-coordinate has changed sign while the $x$-coordinates remain the same: $(1,1)\to(1,-1)$, etc. This is a reflection in the $x$-axis.

questions.stem: Shape $P$ is mapped to shape $Q$. Shape $Q$ is similar to $P$ but larger and on the opposite side of a point. What type of transformation is this?

options.text: Enlargement with a negative scale factor

questions.explanation: The image is larger (so a scale factor with $|k| > 1$) and on the opposite side of a point (so the scale factor is negative). This describes an enlargement with a negative scale factor.
